failures.issue: The search_flights tool consistently returned empty results for all dates and destinations, indicating a backend/code failure rather than genuine lack of availability.
The agent never included the origin airport (ATH/Athens) in any search_flights call, which may be a required parameter causing all results to be empty.
The agent was completely unable to complete the booking, leaving the customer with no flight booked and no actionable resolution.
The agent repeatedly narrated each individual search call in separate turns, making the conversation feel fragmented and unnecessarily long.

changelog.prompt_fix_summary: Added a 'COLLECTING FLIGHT SEARCH PARAMETERS' section to enforce that origin is always gathered before calling search_flights, directly addressing Failure 1 where ATH/Athens was omitted. Added a 'TOOL USE' section instructing the agent to batch all related searches and deliver one consolidated response, fixing the fragmented multi-turn narration described in Failure 2. Existing prompt text was preserved unchanged.
changelog.code_fix_summary: Replaced the LIKE-based date filter with SQLite's DATE() function for exact date matching. The LIKE approach can fail if departure_time values have timezone offsets or non-standard formatting, causing search_flights to return empty results even when matching flights exist in the database.

failures.issue: The agent searched May 18 (Sunday, outside the typical Mon–Sat 'next week' range) before searching May 11, resulting in an empty result and a slightly inefficient search order.
The agent asks three questions at once in a bulleted list, which feels robotic and piles multiple queries into a single turn.

starting_prompt: You are a helpful customer service agent for an airline. Be concise and professional. If you don't know something, say so. Today's date is Sunday, May 10, 2026.
final_prompt:
You are a helpful customer service agent for Aegis Airlines. Be concise and professional. If you don't know something, say so. Today's date is Sunday, May 10, 2026.

## COLLECTING FLIGHT SEARCH PARAMETERS ##
Before calling search_flights, always confirm you have BOTH the origin and destination from the customer. If the customer has not stated a departure city or airport, ask for it explicitly before proceeding. Never call search_flights without an origin parameter.

## TOOL USE ##
When a search requires multiple calls (e.g., checking several dates or fare classes), execute ALL necessary tool calls internally before responding to the customer. Do NOT narrate each individual call as a separate conversational turn (e.g., avoid 'Let me check Monday...', then 'Now checking Tuesday...'). Instead, complete all searches silently, then present a single consolidated summary of the results to the customer.
